entries.clue: Regularly putting out germiest mince – it’ll make you sick (6)

indicators.note: 'regularly' takes every other letter, and 'putting out' says those letters are what comes out

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th, 6th… letters: gEr mIe sT mInCe

annotation.surface: A warning about mince so full of germs that eating it will make you ill.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits wordplay from definition; 'mince' and 'sick' both pull towards an anagram, but the letters are simply every second one of the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to make you vomit.

entries.clue: Is due to receive millions following Mike’s bluff (9)

indicators.note: the IS IN FOR + M chunk comes after (follows) M for Mike

blocks.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet's word for the letter M
'in for' = due to receive, as in 'in for a surprise'

annotation.surface: Someone about to come into millions, and a man called Mike who may be bluffing about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mike's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is really 'is' joining wordplay to definition. 'Bluff' is a verb here: to deceive.
annotation.definitionFit: To bluff someone is to mislead them, which is to misinform them.

entries.clue: Swimmer needs to dry back (6)

indicators.note: to go back is to return the way you came, so the letters are read from the end

annotation.surface: A swimmer climbing out of the pool and needing to towel off their back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person, but in crosswords it is often a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: any fish is a swimmer, and this flatfish is one instance.

entries.clue: Perhaps lower fences were in front of abandoned … (6,3)

indicators.note: the CALF encloses LED + OF, as a fence surrounds a field

blocks.note: a lower is something that lows (moos), such as a calf; 'perhaps' flags the example

annotation.surface: Something about fences being lowered in front of an abandoned site, trailing off into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is read as 'less high' but means 'one who lows', a cow or calf. The ellipsis carries the sentence on into 5 down; this clue ends at 'abandoned'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sporting sense: a match stopped for rain is both.

entries.clue: Greek river carp (6)

blocks.note: the Ouse is a river in England

annotation.surface: A carp swimming in a river in Greece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish finishing the river picture, but it is the verb: to complain.
annotation.definitionFit: To carp and to grouse both mean to grumble.

entries.clue: … roads – oddly doctor engages clutch (5)

indicators.note: takes the odd-numbered letters of 'roads'
GP takes RAS inside, as gears engage

blocks.note: GP = general practitioner, a family doctor

annotation.surface: Continuing 4 down: on abandoned roads, a driver engages the clutch.
annotation.walkthrough: The motoring picture makes 'clutch' a car pedal and 'engages' a gear change; clutch is really the verb, to grip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to seize and hold tight.

entries.clue: Public describing cabinet – mostly dull (8)

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so OVERT goes round CAS
drops the last letter of CASE

blocks.note: a case (display cabinet) with its last letter gone

annotation.surface: A remark that public accounts of the government Cabinet are mostly boring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests government ministers, but it is a piece of furniture. 'Dull' describes the weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A weather synonym: a sky covered in grey cloud is described both ways.

entries.clue: Dark horses kept together wanting support ultimately (5)

indicators.note: lacking: STABLE loses a letter
the letter lost is the last one of 'support'

blocks.note: a stable is a set of horses housed together

annotation.surface: Dark horses are kept together in one yard but lack support.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' is a ready-made phrase that hides the split: 'Dark' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Sable is black, the heraldic word for dark.

entries.clue: Get wind of court procedure that is void after one leaves (7)

indicators.note: one = I, which leaves MISTRIAL

blocks.note: a mistrial is a trial declared void

annotation.surface: Someone hearing about a botched court case, 'getting wind of' it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get wind of' reads as one idiom meaning 'hear about'; the definition is just 'wind'.
annotation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France.

entries.clue: Sadness of first lady catching her only lad, 15, breaking in (11)

indicators.note: C + HOL break into MELANIA
15 down's answer is INITIALLY: take the first letters

blocks.note: c = caught in cricket scorecards, so catching gives C

annotation.surface: A first lady saddened as her only son breaks in on her.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 15 stands for the word INITIALLY, which is the first-letters instruction. 'First lady' could be Eve, but the one needed is Melania.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly literary: the old medical name for a deep, lasting low mood.

entries.clue: Writer joining electronics firm, Sharp (7)

indicators.note: a new recruit joining a firm is added to it, so the pen is attached to the company

blocks.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen

annotation.surface: A writer taking a job at the electronics company Sharp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like the name of the firm, and 'writer' like an author; the writer is a pen and Sharp is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym for the tone of a remark or wit: cutting, tart, from the Latin for sour.

entries.clue: Actress cooked sauce up – it’s sweet (6,5)

indicators.note: ACTRESS is cooked into new letters
in a down clue, RAGU read upwards

annotation.surface: An actress in the kitchen whipping up a sweet sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: ACTRESS rearranges to CASTERS, supplying the S of SUGAR too, so the split falls inside the second word.
annotation.definitionFit: Caster sugar is fine white sugar used in baking, so something sweet.

entries.clue: Keep online costs high and make profit (4,4,7)

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated: the letters are out of their right minds

annotation.surface: Business advice: charge a lot for your online service and rake in money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High' reads as the level of the costs; it is the anagram signal, in its drugged sense.
annotation.definitionFit: To line one's pockets is to make money, usually dishonestly.

entries.clue: Number 10 on table … and 11 (4)

indicators.note: points to 11 across, LINE ONE'S POCKETS, where the answer sits inside

annotation.surface: A house number on a table, like a seating plan at a wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: The table is the periodic table, and number 10 is the atomic number. The ellipsis ties this to 11 across, whose answer hides the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Neon has atomic number 10, so it is element number 10 on the periodic table.

entries.clue: Controlling gang I’ve put on ship (10)

indicators.note: in an across answer, IVE is placed on (after) SS

annotation.surface: A domineering gang boss getting a crew aboard a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'put on' means placed after; SS for ship is a standing crossword abbreviation worth learning.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym from relationships: a partner who wants to own and direct the other.

entries.clue: What about two weeks on board small boat is awry? (4-5)

indicators.note: about means around, as in 'walls about the town', so one piece surrounds the other
EWWH is taken aboard the boat, inside SKIFF

blocks.note: a skiff is a small rowing boat

annotation.surface: Asking what has gone wrong with a fortnight spent on a small boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'What' look like the start of a question, but it is EH.
annotation.definitionFit: Skew-whiff is informal British for crooked, askew, awry.

entries.clue: One-nil: Italy after playing first (9)

indicators.note: the letters of I, NIL and ITALY are played about

annotation.surface: A football score: one-nil to Italy, after they played first.
annotation.walkthrough: The scoreline hides the anagram; 'first' is an adverb, like INITIALLY.
annotation.definitionFit: First, as in 'first, preheat the oven', means initially.

entries.clue: Plug books including present for fan (8)

indicators.note: NT includes HERE… more exactly, HERE sits between AD and NT

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad
here = present, as in a roll call
NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: An author plugging their books, with a present thrown in for a fan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift for the fan, but it is the roll-call answer. 'Books' is the New Testament, a standard crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who sticks to a cause or leader, from the Latin for cling.

entries.clue: Person lacking an identity – if that is right, it changes the atmosphere (10)

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: ID = identity, as on an ID card

annotation.surface: A person with no sense of self who could change the mood of a whole room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lacking an identity' reads as one phrase, but the AN belongs to the deletion and 'identity' is the separate ID. 'Atmosphere' means the air in the room, not the mood.
annotation.definitionFit: A humidifier adds moisture to the air, changing a room's atmosphere.

entries.clue: Book is framing American prejudice (4)

indicators.note: IS goes round A like a frame

annotation.surface: A book accused of stitching up an American with a prejudiced portrayal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Framing' plays on setting someone up; here it just means surrounding.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are a leaning judgement formed in advance.

entries.clue: Hesitate seeing detective on the run (6)

blocks.note: in a down clue, DI sits on top of what follows

annotation.surface: Hesitating on spotting a detective while on the run from the law.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the run' is the fugitive's phrase, but it splits into ON (placement), THE, and R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, dither being the more informal, fussy word for wavering.

entries.clue: I want gin I spilled on toilet attendants? (6-2-7)

indicators.note: the letters of I WANT GIN I are spilled out and rearranged

blocks.note: the Ladies is a women's toilet in British usage

annotation.surface: A drinker who spilled gin on the toilet attendants and wants more.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the anagram after LADIES. The question mark flags the joke: attendants in a Ladies' toilet as ladies-in-waiting.
annotation.definitionFit: Ladies-in-waiting are women who attend a queen or princess.

entries.clue: Try to discourage – maybe does without half of it (5)

indicators.note: outside: DEER goes round T
keeps one of the two letters of IT

blocks.note: does are female deer; 'maybe' flags the example

annotation.surface: Trying to put someone off, who perhaps manages without half of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as the verb; it is the plural of doe. 'Without' is the old sense, outside.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a deterrent aims to put people off, whether or not it succeeds.

entries.clue: Finally comedy club opens offering humour of a kind (5)

indicators.note: takes the last letter of 'comedy'
IRON opens the answer, coming before Y

blocks.note: an iron is a golf club

annotation.surface: A comedy club finally opening its doors to offer a certain kind of humour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Comedy club' reads as one venue; 'club' is really a golf club.
annotation.definitionFit: Irony is a kind of humour that says the opposite of what is meant.

entries.clue: Sorting trade discount essentially for particular style (3,4)

indicators.note: TRADE is sorted into a new order
takes the core, the middle letters, of 'discount'

annotation.surface: Arranging a trade discount for a customer with a particular taste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trade discount' reads as one business term; it splits into fodder and a source of middle letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the geometric design movement of the 1920s and 30s is one named style.

entries.clue: Find that clerk unwrapping everything to get medical device (7)

indicators.note: every word loses its outside letters, its wrapping

annotation.surface: An instruction to find the clerk who is unwrapping all the medical supplies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unwrapping everything' sounds like opening parcels; it strips the first and last letter from each of the three words.
annotation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device for breathing in medicine, used for asthma.

entries.clue: Somewhat attractive (6)

blocks.note: an adverb meaning fairly or quite

annotation.surface: A lukewarm compliment: somewhat attractive.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, adverb then adjective; PRETTY is 'fairly' in 'pretty good' and 'good-looking' in 'a pretty face'.
annotation.definitionFit: Pretty means both fairly (adverb) and attractive (adjective).

entries.clue: Attempts to get a yes on vacation (6)

indicators.note: YES is vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: for = in order to get, as in 'queue for tickets'

annotation.surface: Holidaymakers trying to get someone to say yes while away on vacation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' looks like a holiday; in crosswords it means a word emptied of its inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Forays are attempts at something new, as in a foray into politics.
